bull.b: The Comerica integration is already improving profitability and efficiency despite the scale of the conversion. Successful systems migration, client retention and expected remaining expense synergies can strengthen earnings power and competitive scale over the next several quarters.

Growing core deposits provide a durable funding base for loan expansion and reduce reliance on wholesale borrowing. Deposit gains across the retail footprint, combined with lower wholesale funding, improve liquidity flexibility and support more resilient banking economics.

bull.t: Diversified fee revenue and innovation banking
bull.b: Expansion in wealth, commercial banking, mortgage and payments broadens revenue beyond interest spreads, while Innovation Banking adds a targeted growth platform. This mix can improve revenue resilience and deepen relationships with businesses across their growth stages.

bear.b: Higher deposit pricing and tighter commercial and auto lending spreads can constrain the benefit of loan and net interest income growth. Persistent funding competition would pressure spread profitability and make future earnings more dependent on volume and fee expansion.

The remaining merger-related charges will continue to weigh on reported expenses and earnings during the integration period. Although synergies are emerging, the substantial cost burden creates execution risk and delays the full conversion of scale benefits into bottom-line results.

bear.t: Credit quality and capital efficiency watchpoints
bear.b: Higher nonperforming assets indicate some deterioration in credit performance, while lower ROE shows that the enlarged equity base is producing less return than in prior years. Together, these trends could limit capital efficiency if they persist through the integration cycle.
